#1354. Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

This touch and finish from Jurriën Timber 😮‍💨 Arsenal lead against Lille! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/L2B6YsNDXo

“We had moments in the game in the first half … [when] we arrived in very dangerous positions,” Arteta said. “With a lot of advantage, our technical quality wasn’t good enough to deliver moments of real threat and especially to be able to sustain the attack, so we allowed certain transitions.” He said that he made some changes at half-time, as managers are wont to do, and that things improved but the real change was clear when he made the substitutions.

“It was a joy to watch,” Arteta said. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Three different players and a lot of players participating in those goals, so overall very, very happy.” He had played Myles Lewis-Skelly at left-back again to give Riccardo Calafiori a rest. Saka had been ill during the week and not in a position to start.

In the opposing technical area was Davide Ancelotti, the 37-year-old son of Carlo, with his father’s trademark slow amble to the edge of the technical area. Young Ancelotti had drilled his team well, but once they were exposed to the high-pace recovery and sharp passing geometry of the Arsenal substitutes there was to be no coming back. Saka made the second for Eberechi Eze who had started the game on the left and the Arsenal No 7 scored the third himself. The home fans sang again about being champions of England and they certainly looked the part.

It didn't take Arsenal long to double their lead ⚡️ Eberechi Eze scores to make it 2-0 🎯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/BVMieESgbi

It took a while. Arteta got ever more sour in his dealings with Richard Hempel, the giant German fourth official. Bruno Guimarães hustled as best he could in midfield and might have won a penalty. But essentially Arsenal lacked the subtle attacking edge that distinguishes the best from the rest in this competition. You could see it immediately in the way that Odegaard hunted for the ball for the second goal and then turned urgently to attack Lille. The third goal was a passing sequence from Saka to Odegaard to Havertz and back to Saka for the finish.

Arsenal are on fire now 🔥 Bukayo Saka extends their lead to 3-0 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ZbCmhueaXo

The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Guimarães had two chances in the first half. Lille’s Japan international Ayase Ueda had a goal disallowed for offside. Guimarães would have a further penalty appeal before the hour as Arteta began to consider the substitutions.

Lille thought they'd taken the lead at the Emirates, but it's ruled out for offside ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/c0k49kH5sn

The goals came quickly after the hour. First Timber’s delicately lifted chip over Ozer from Madueke’s ball. Eze ran onto a left-foot shot from Saka’s pass to score four minutes later. Soon after that Arsenal sliced Lille open a third time and Saka took a touch in the area before finishing.

Arteta starts his press conference with a tribute to Ken Friar: "There are people in football clubs that create an identity, create values and have a vision to create a future. The legacy that Ken is going to leave, to all of us and to our club, is going to be forever."

A few things tactically: one adjustment attacking, one defending. But especially, that we had to increase the technical level. At this level, the teams are really well organised. We gave simple ball;s away, bad touches mistimed things. When we delivered the ball into the box it wasn’t the right area so we get caught, especially delivering from the right and [Lille] transition on the left.

The moment we started to do that better, we could counter-press, and start to play into the opposition’s box, and with the quality that we have we made a real difference there.

I had some moments in the first half but second half I had more. First touch was good, which was half the job, and then Noni [Madueke] was screaming “shoot” so I thought OK I have to shoot. And then yeah it went in nice.

I wasn’t thinking too much. I saw the goal and thought I need to shoot. We needed that first goal, we were playing well just needed the goal. Happy to get that for the team.

Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s draw at Viking, meaning he will miss next week’s game against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

Since returning to the competition under Arteta in 2023, they have won all 12 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Four of those goals came in effective dead rubbers against PSV in the 2025 last-16 (after Arsenal won 7-1 in Eindhoven) and against Kairat Almaty in the final game of last season’s league phase.

So in home Champions League games that matter, they have conceded just four goals in 18 matches: Serge Gnarby and Harry Kane for Bayern in the 2024 quarter-final, Ousmane Dembele in the 2025 semi-final and Lennart Karl for Bayern in last season’s league phase.

Just like against Leeds at the weekend, Arsenal’s closing half hour was their best spell of the match. This was not their most fluent or creative performance, but sheer weight of pressure told and Lille cracked. The away team could not get out of their defensive third after half time, and after Timber’s goal the class of Saka, Havertz and Odegaard from the bench took over.

Two wins from two in the Champions League for Arsenal, joining Sporting and Barcelona as the teams with a 100 per cent record.

Just the three minutes of added time to play. Havertz has just been booked for catching the goalkeeper Ozer who was dallying on the ball.

Odegaard with a delightful first-time pass around the corner to Dowman, but the youngster cut inside looking for his goal and his shot was blocked. Maybe he could have looked for Saka across goal.

Arsenal happy to usher this game to a conclusion now. Dowman had one chance to run at the Lille defence from the right, but he played a pass expected a Havertz run that never came.

Max Dowman is now on for Eze. Saka will finish the game on the left, with Dowman on the right.

An extra treat for the Arsenal fans who have not made an early exit: Mikel Arteta is about to bring on Max Dowman. This feels like a presentable opportunity for a first Champions League goal, Lille have been non-existent in this half.

The yellow card is coming out for Lille’s Goffi, who catches the inside of Eze’s ankle with his studs. The tackle did not quite have enough force to be worthy of a red card.

Bruno Guimaraes stings the palms of Ozer with a strike from the edge of the box, when perhaps he could have looked for Saka.

Olivier Giroud is on now for Lille, and he receives a standing ovation from most of the Emirates. A rarity when a former player returns.

Arteta has made another change: Ben White replaces Timber.

Big block by Ezri Konsa to help preserve Arsenal’s clean sheet, but Lille are still to have a shot on target. They were competitive in the first half, but have found the intensity too much too handle in the second 45 minutes.

That will answer some questions about his finishing, Arsenal’s No 7 rolls the ball into the bottom corner and they have scored three in seven second-half minutes. Slick combination play involving Timber, Odegaard and Havertz down the right, and the German played a cute ball back to Saka and he finished in style.

Arsenal have scored quite a few lovely team goals so far this season, including against Leeds United a few days ago. That was another one. The combination of Saka, Odegaard and Havertz was too much for Lille to handle. The arrival of those three substitutes has massively enhanced Arsenal’s attack.

Arsenal are on fire now 🔥 Bukayo Saka extends their lead to 3-0 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ZbCmhueaXo

Eze goes close again with poked finish which the goalkeeper palms away from danger. Lille finished their league game with 10 at the weekend, and it looks like they legs have completely gone.

Bentaleb gives the ball away in midfield, and it is all too easy for Arsenal to find Saka in space down the right. He picks out Eze at the edge of the box, and his left-footed strike took a slight deflection and flew into the bottom corner.

It didn't take Arsenal long to double their lead ⚡️ Eberechi Eze scores to make it 2-0 🎯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/BVMieESgbi

Here come the changes regardless: Saka, Havertz and Odegaard replace Madueke, Merino and Gyokeres.

Just as I say there is no space in the Lille box, Timber creates some with a superb first touch around the corner to his right before lifting the ball over the Lille goalkeeper Ozer. A finish worthy of any striker. Would it be harsh to say it’s the kind of finish Arsenal’s actual striker has never looked like providing?

Arsenal have been working the ball into those positions inside the penalty box all game long, and finally it brings the breakthrough. There aren’t many defenders who can control and finish as cleanly as that, in a penalty box as crowded as it was there. A classy goal.

This touch and finish from Jurriën Timber 😮‍💨 Arsenal lead against Lille! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/L2B6YsNDXo

Odegaard and Saka are getting themselves ready on the bench, the changes are incoming.

Excellent recovery from Rice to snuff a Lille break, the ball just keeps coming back at the French side.

If anything, Arsenal have been almost too dominant. The game is a 10vs10 on the edge of the Lille box with no space.

Bruno Guimaraes has been Arsenal’s most enterprising player, and he has just gone down looking for a penalty. I think he was looking for it, and the on-field decision of no penalty stands. The defender may have trailed a leg, but it was unconvincing attempt from Guimaraes. Sam disagrees though!

I’m surprised that wasn’t given as a penalty. Looked like a clear movement into Bruno’s path, with no contact on the ball.

Arsenal completely dominant now, without producing a final pass or shot of any great quality. Lille’s goalkeeper Ozer has not had to make a save in this spell despite all this possession. Lille penalised for taking too long over a throw, before Madueke’s shot is deflected through to Ozer.

Very obvious foul conceded by Gyokeres at the edge of the Lille box just as Arsenal were probing again. Then Bruno Guimaraes wins a free-kick in a crossing position left of centre. They are making hard work of it, but Arsenal do have Lille penned in.

Arsenal play a short one, and Timber is then flagged offside as Eze tries to find him with a reverse pass.

Bruno Guimarães loves a fist-pump to the home supporters and he’s produced a couple here tonight, in an attempt to lift the atmosphere. That’s not to say it’s a bad atmosphere but there is frustration building.

It took a long time for the referee to blow his whistle, but he gives a foul against Madueke on Perraud and Lille can clear their lines after a couple of minutes of Arsenal pressure.

All Arsenal so far in the second half, and they work the ball well into Guimaraes at the edge of the area but he slices his shot wide with his weaker left foot. Feels like the home team are getting closer, though.

Arsenal with another Madueke corner, as they try to apply the pressure. Good delivery into the six-yard box, and it flicks off a Lille head for another corner on the far side. Rice to take.

Headed away. Clever Eze reverse pass to Timber, but crossing with his left foot is not his strong suit and he slices behind.

Arsenal win a corner inside 30 seconds of the second half after a Timber burst forward.

Slow starts have been a theme of late for Arsenal.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not issue Richardson with a caution.

Lille said the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

“LOSC is exploring all possible legal avenues and reserves the right to take any legal action necessary to obtain compensation for its losses,” the ​club said. “It will support Tiago in ‌any steps he decides to take to defend his rights.”

Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Olivier Giroud back at the Emirates ❤️ https://t.co/TPBgcNDsVW

Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel)

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#1352. Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool: Sloppy Reds wilt in Turkey again as Dirk Kuyt masterminds famous Champions League win against his error-strewn old side

Published: 14:54 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:15 EDT, 5 November 2026

The mad metropolis of Istanbul was the setting for one of Liverpool’s greatest nights, when this storied old club won the 2005 Champions League final down the road at the Ataturk Stadium – but right now fans will be glad to see the back of Turkey for a while.

For the third time in just over 13 months, the English giants have travelled to the bustling hub on the banks of the Bosphorus only to wilt amid the deafening noise of a Turkish football stadium.

They lost twice to Galatasaray last season and now, over the river to the Asian side of the intercontinental Istanbul, Liverpool fell flat at the hands of Fenerbahce – thanks to two Englishmen and a friend-turned-foe in the dugout.

Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown, born in Bradford and Birmingham respectively, both scored for Fenerbahce before Vedat Muriqi scored a winner as caretaker manager Dirk Kuyt, once a cult hero at Anfield, recorded a win in his final game in the dugout.

He will soon be replaced by ex-Newcastle and 101-cap Turkey midfielder Emre Belozoglu but Kuyt will not be forgetting this evening in a hurry in front of a raucous, hostile crowd in the district of Kadikoy.

As for Liverpool, who jetted home straight after the game and were due to land around 2am English time, they and boss Andoni Iraola were just glad to get out of Turkey, probably with their ears still ringing.

It was a poor night for Liverpool as they went down 3-2 against Fenerbahce in Istanbul

Andoni Iraola's side let a second-half lead slip and there were some terrible errors

Archie Brown sunk to his knees in celebration at full-time as the home crowd erupted

Trey Nyoni had scored his first goal in professional football and then Alexander Isak headed home to put Liverpool 2-1 up two minutes after coming on as a substitute but they were undone by sloppy defensive errors.

That will give Iraola plenty to ponder in the coming weeks given his side have conceded nine goals in their last three European games, all to opposition that would not be counted as part of the continent’s best in LASK, Villarreal and now Fenerbahce.

Aside from a UEFA Super Cup triumph over Chelsea at the home of Besiktas in 2019, Liverpool have struggled in this country and their last Turkish delight came against Trabzonspor, who now employ a certain Mohamed Salah, back in 2010.

Fenerbahce and Kuyt celebrated a famous win – as did around 45,000 home fans who produced deafening whistles every time Liverpool had the ball.

It was a true attack on the senses and Iraola’s side felt it, with several passes going astray as Kuyt’s men had the best of the first-half action and were unlucky to go into the break level at 1-1.

Liverpool had gone ahead on 25 minutes through Nyoni’s first goal in professional football, when a header from English full back Brown fell straight into the path of the Reds midfielder, who charged on to the ball like he was Steven Gerrard.

He needed a deflection off defender Kojo Peprah Oppong but cared not a jot as his volley ended up beating former Manchester City man Ederson.

It continued a stellar season for 19-year-old Nyoni, who has had a fairytale week that included a first Premier League start, first professional goal and also talks over a bumper new contract. To say it would be deserved would be the understatement of the season.

Trey Nyoni opened the scoring for the Reds but his goal came in a losing effort

Alexander Isak headed Liverpool back in front after some terrible Fenerbahce defending

FENERBAHCE (4-3-3): Ederson 5; Semedo 5 (Muldur 75), Skriniar 6, Peprah 6, BROWN 8; Guendouzi 7, Kante 7, Yuksek 5; Greenwood 8 (Aydin 89), Lukaku 7 (Muriqi 63, 6), Kahveci 7 (Arturkoglu 75).

Subs not used: Cetin, Gunok, Efe Demir, Mercan, Elmaz, Nene, Mimovic.

Scorers: Greenwood 29, Brown 73, Muriqi 79.

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 4; Gomez 5 (Wirtz 66, 6), Jacquet 5, Van Dijk 4, Tsimikas 4 (Kerkez 76); Nyoni 8 (Koumas 85), Mac Allister 7; Munoz 5 (Isak 66, 6), Szoboszlai 5, Ngumoha 7 (Gakpo 67, 6); Barcola 5.

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Araujo, Chambers, McConnell, Danns.

Nyoni’s goal, in theory, should have helped Liverpool settle. As it was, it did anything but.

Fenerbahce came out roaring and hit the bar instantly through Irfan Can Kahveci. With the next attack, they were level, just four minutes after falling behind.

Just like Liverpool’s goal, the Turkish side needed a hefty deflection to help them. Greenwood took a free-kick from 25 yards, Jeremy Jacquet turned his back on it and foxed Alisson. Two Brazilian goalkeepers, two wicked deflections that neither could do anything about.

Alisson was the best away player on the pitch in that opening 45 minutes, thwarting Greenwood, the brute force of Romelu Lukaku and fellow former Premier League favourite N'Golo Kante, who is now 35 but still has the energy of the young whippersnapper we all knew and loved.

Iraola turned to his bench with a £285million triple-change and two of them combined just minutes later, Cody Gakpo crossing for Isak to head home his seventh of the season.

But just as when they went 1-0 ahead, Liverpool retreated and invited pressure. A Kante cross was not dealt with by Gakpo and Brown could ghost in at the back post to score.

Then, on 79 minutes, Muriqi thumped home a header to put Fenerbahce 3-2 up and on their way to a memorable night.

Liverpool, who would have taken a huge step towards qualification with a win here, still have work to do.

#1351. Carrick’s United are in crisis and now spotlight is on Wilcox

Michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn

They certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a big game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

United cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

It looks like a bit of an agenda because it wasn’t a poor performance.

[How do you sum up the performance?] Really poor, Really poor. I have to control myself a lot. Sometimes it’s a mirror of the reflection of how our club is. We had a fantastic season last season but in order to compete we needed to buy more players. Many teams buy many players and Atletico Madrid did. They have an amazing team and deserved to win today.

I expected more. [Are you saying you expected more investment in the squad this summer?] Yes 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest. As players we have to do more but it is important to make a strong squad to be ready for for this kind of night.

In general, in general [should you have invested more in defence and attack given all the midfielders]. Last season we made a strong base to build an amazing team. It’s annoying and disappointing coming here and trying to get a result.

I don’t think so [was the manager backed?] He does his best. You can’t [live on] what you did last season. Every season is different. You can’t stay with what you did last season. The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don’t change next season is a big problem.

It’s changing, changing, changing the manager [after a poor run]. But what about other areas? I can’t say more.

Tonight is it easy to say the coach, easy to say the players [are at fault]. But we have to look at other areas.

So far this season there have been more times when the performances have been worse than the results. This was the other way round but there is a sizeable quality gap between Carrick’s squad and the company they are keeping. They can point to a soft red card but they still shot themselves in the foot with their doziness in the first minute and squandering the good chances they created.

Maguire strays offside when Mount, from the short corner, tries to pick him out at the back post.

Amad, now on the right, tries to dribble past Grimaldo who wins the ball off him but Atletico give it straight back. Man Utd work it into the box for Zirkzee to cushion and then dither so long over a shot he has to lay it off to Cunha who hits it straight at the keeper with two-thirds of the goal vacant. Oblak turns it wide.

Five minutes of stoppage time are signalled.

Alan Shearer says there has been improvement tonight since Saturday. “They have stuck together and have not been outrun.” This is a very low bar but OK. He goes on to say that the glaring weakness is not attitude but a lack of finishing quality.

And Le Normand is booked within seconds of his introduction for a tug of the shirt.

Dalot lofts a deep cross way beyond Zirkzee. I think Dalot encompasses Man Utd’s recruitment over the past eight years or so in that it’s hard to see any progression or improvement since the day they signed him. Maybe he always had a low ceiling. But where on earth is the coaching?

Manchester United have had their chances but they have lacked an elite or even merely decent finisher.

Atletico 2 Man Utd 0 (Lookman)  The three men were not enough and were carved apart by one pass from the left, from Grimaldo I think to David who opened his body to fire a shot towards the bottom right. Lammens dives to save but Lookman is Johnny on the spot to beat Dalot to the rebound and score.

Carrick now has three at the back after the sending off.

He places his hand on his shoulder and let it creep down on to Lookman’s chest as the former Everton winger tried to run clear from 40 yards.

The referee is sent to the screen to look again at Yoro’s contact on Lookman, the hand on the shoulder. Was it DOGSO, denial of a goalscoring opportunity. It was very weak.

Fernandes plays the corner to Amad standing to the left of the D, who rolls it halfway back and the captain wraps his foot around a blistering shot that thumps into the crossbar.

Cute pass from Heaven sends Amad down the left but still no target for him to find and he has to settle for a corner.

Mount wins the ball off Baena, passes out to Dalot on the right and he squares it to Bruno Fernandes. The captain opens his foot to shoot and the ball deflects off Zirkzee, killing its power. Oblak flops forward to gather.

Amad is on the left, Mbeumo to the right and Zirkzee down the middle with Fernandes tucked behind.

After Baena shoots at Lammens, Man Utd make a triple substitution:

Amad → RashfordMount → BalebaZirkzee → Tielemans.

Cross from the right. Bruno whips it around the left-back but Mbeumo, not really a centre-forward, held his line rather than running across Romero’s shoulder and that allows the former Spurs captain to get there first. Bruno signals his frustration.

Pubill goes to right-back and Llorente moves into midfield.

Baena cuts in off the left to shoot with his right, trying to curl it into the top right but the ball will not bend to his will and ends up being far to straight. He was looking for a banana bend and ended up with a cucumber.

Manchester United carve Atletico open with a simple long, left to right diagonal pass that Romero misjudges. Fernandes leaps to try to hook it on the volley over Oblak but instead steers it wide of the left post.

Terrific pass from Barrios picks out Alvarez on the left of the box and he thumps his shot into the post. Lammens, who dived to try to stop it, is stranded but Martinez is there to scramble the ball behind as it rebounded into the six-yard box.

Rashford slips Tielemans down the left and he stands up a cross that Oblan can pick out of the sky unmolested. Might be worth a gamble if they had Sesko to bring on.

Baena arrows a long cross straight at Lammens.

Good work from Baleba to win the ball off Barrios as the arrowhead of a three-man press but his chip down the left finds Rashford offside.

A foul on Fernandes is followed 40 seconds later by Rashford being penalised for trying to get past Simeone by holding his shoulder.

Yoro pushes high into the press and dispossesses Grimaldo and squares it to Bruno Fernandes. He clips a pass towards the penalty spot but too far from Mbeumo. Fernandes is patently unfit. I know he’s the captain/talisman but he is not very effective tonight.

No doubt Manchester United have improved and created a couple of chances for Mbeumo and one for Rashford. Baleba should really have buried that free back-post header from the corner, too. And that second Atletico ‘goal’ being disallowed was a real tonic on the stroke of half-time. Kudos fro not crumbling. But I wouldn’t be surprised if Baena, Alvarez and Lee carved them open again.

Tielemans is penalised for a foul on Cardoso who has no time to do anything with the free-kick in his own half.

The ball hit Llorente’s hand as it bounced back off Heaven in a block tackle before Cardoso swept a right-foot shot into the bottom left.

No goal! He gained an advantage and the referee chalks it off.

Man United survive... just 😅 Atletico's second of the night is ruled out by VAR 📺 https://t.co/MEJK3aNUBG

Atletico 2 Man Utd 0 (Jonny Cardoso)  VAR check for handball.

Alvarez picks up his head and spanks a right-foot shot from 25 yards over the bar.

The home crowd gasps as Baena traps a 40-yard crossfield chip on his thigh and fizzes a pass inside to Alvarez who gives it right back to him but Yoro had stuck with him and stops the danger.

Atletico have a free-kick on the right just inside the Man Utd half for Heaven’s shove. They go back to switch it up the left, then back over to the right.

Man Utd let Baena run at them again, straight down the inside-left channel, until they finally get a tackle in. They are so open to straight runs it is truly bizarre. The defenders just won’t push up to engage. Then again they were high for the goal so I suppose they know how vulnerable they are to pace.

Diego Simeone is booked for asking for a card for Santos after he tripped Jonny Cardoso who had juts nutmegged him.

Llorente overhits a cross a yard or so in from the byline down the right but Grimaldo retrieves it and works the ball back across into the middle. Tielemans picks it off but has no outlet and is squeezed until he coughs the ball up.

Rashford’s control on the right takes him past one man but then, instead of crossing, he tries to take on Grimaldo who stands between him and the ball and buys a foul.

The tenacious Barrios wins a corner on the left that Baena takes and Martinez clears at the back post.

Fernandes chips a free-kick from just inside the Atletico half straight to Oblak.

Atletico free-kick 20 yards out on the left for a clumsy Martinez foul. Grimaldo, who was in Spain’s World Cup-winning squad, takes and curls it on to the roof of the net, scraping the top of the crossbar.

Bruno Fernandes whips the corner from the left to the back post and Baleba, unmarked, peels round the back to head it straight down Oblak’s throat.

Mbeumo pounces on Romero’s weak pass, he plays a one-two with Tielemans and strides into the box to shoot from an angle of about 45 degrees on the left. Oblak gets down smartly to turn it behind.

Mbuemo goes CLOSE to an equaliser for United! 🤏 https://t.co/m7HwWIXvh0

United have settled down a little now after that horrific start and they’ve fashioned good chances for Mbeumo and Rashford. There’s that feeling, though, that Atletico could just run through the gears at any moment. Some of their movement is so good.

Bruno Fernandes scoops a cross from the right to the back post. Man Utd are outnumbered 6-2 in the Atletico box and Simeone calmly chests it back to the seemingly ageless Oblak.

One downside of this front three is that they are allowing, by design, I think, Atletico’s central defenders to stroke the ball around without putting them under any pressure.

The rotation of Atletico’s forwards – Baena, Alvarez, Lee and Simeone – is dragging the Man Utd defenders out of position. They still need more help from Baleba and Santos.

Vast improvement in the last few minutes from the away side and now Martinez wedges a chip over Romero and Llorente into the path of Rashford’s superb run. As the ball skipped up in his stride, he tries to put his laces through a volley but fails to make the right connection. As Alan Shearer says, it was begging for a side-foot finish but he opted for power.

Chance for Mbeumo whose control and touch but him an opportunity to shoot from 16 yards. He wraps his left instep around the shot and beats the keeper but a touch off Llorenete takes it past the post for a corner that Atlético defend solidly.

Mbeumo sprays a pass up the left for Rashford to chase and he lengthens his stride into a gallop. But Llorente is just as quick, stalks his every step and makes the tackle.

Baena, Johnny and Barrios zip passes between them in a triangle to take Dalot out of the game but back comes Santos to block Baena’s cross.

Baena has the freedom of the field and Man Utd are not picking him up. He drops off Santos to shoot from 20 yards but Yoro gets in the way. He ghosts into space and with Grimaldo pushing high on the left also, he’s too much for Dalot to handle.

Could not have got off to a worse start. No doubt the lack of understanding between the players contributed to that mix-up.

Atlético 1 Man Utd 0 (Barrios) A goal on 53 seconds to puncture Manchester United’s balloon. A diagonal pass from right to left after an error from Baleba gives Baena the chance to sprint at Yoro and go past him. He darts down the inside left, squares it to Barrios who scuffs a shot that nonetheless messes up the timing of Heaven’s attempt at a sliding block, takes a nick off the defender and goes in.

Deafening whistles before kick-off. It’s not a place for the faint of heart the Metropolitano.

The last time this United defence started together (Leeds in January), the manager (Ruben Amorim) was sacked the next day. That is not a fate that awaits Carrick but it’s not a good omen either. It looks like Heaven will be at left back with Dalot at right back and Yoro in the middle with Martinez.

I have read opinions over the last few minutes that Heaven is at left-back and Dalot at right-back, Yoro is at right-back and Dalot at left and that Dalot is on the right and Martínez on the left. Also some speculation that Bruno Fernandes will play through the middle as a false nine with Mbeumo on the right and another that Rashford will be central with Bruno on the right and Mbeumo on the left. Or, finally, that it’s 4-2-3-1 with the trident of Rashford, Tielemans and Bruno.

Carrick’s team may look like a dog’s dinner but it has at least provoked plenty of debate.

Diego Simeone weighs in on Julian Alvarez, Michael Carrick & tonight's clash vs Manchester United 👀 https://t.co/1E0H7mkFYn

You can read more about Aljoe’s skill here.

This feels a big moment for Carrick and United’s players to answer some of their critics. They have been getting battered from all sides in the last couple of days. Nicky Butt suggested on his podcast that Carrick told him before he got the United job that management “not for me” and “my head’s all over the shop” and that United was the only job he would take. At the very least, those comments are unhelpful and they are thought to have been dimly received internally.

Jamie Carragher offered a lacerating analysis of United’s performance against Spurs on Saturday on Sky Sports on Monday night and suggested things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved if there is not marked improvement. Steven Gerrard questioned why United opted to invest £50m of their summer budget in Andrey Santos, an unused substitute in the last three league games, insisted the back four was not good enough and questioned the work ethic.

And it was interesting to see Carrick alongside his mate Wayne Rooney just now pitchside. Rooney told the Stick to United podcast that captain Bruno Fernandes looks “fed up” and ready to explode at any moment.

It would have been pretty unthinkable for Carrick not to run with a three-man midfield here, not just because of the wide open spaces opponents have exploited this season but when you look at the back line United are fielding. Dalot at left back, two youngsters in Lenny Yoro and Ayden Heaven and a horribly out of form Lisandro Maríinez.

Nor has Senne Lammens looked convincing this term. Matheus Cunha has been dropped – not before time – and I expect to see Fernandes playing off the right. There’s going to a big onus on Rashford on the left. I’m not sure if he is fully fit but he’s going to be important.

It’s fantastic. It’s where we want to be, these games, these competitions. It’s as tough a place as you can come to. They’ve got a really good history in this competition and it’s where we want to come to challenge and test ourselves. We have put ourselves in this position, got a good start at home and now this is our first away game.

We want a reaction, of course. A positive reaction [to Saturday’s poor performance]. It hasn’t gone how we wanted, how we expected so far but it’s been fine margins in some of those games. It can go both ways but the reality is where we are at now.

It’s a fresh night and we’ve got to adapt, we’ve got to adjust in a positive way.

We want a little more control in the game [with three central midfielders]. At times we have been too open. We wanted to make a difference in that way. We’ve made other changes, certain spaces, certain positions.

To be honest it’s not really a big change of shape, personnel maybe but a lot of it is similar. We want more control, a little bit without the ball and a lot more with it. We’re happy with the way we set up.

Look at the last three goals we’ve conceded. They’re a mixed bag, simple goals you can something about. We need to defend better as a whole team .

From their victory over Alaves, Koke, whose mother has died, Le Normand, Lookman and David drop out for Hancko, Lee Kang-in, Baena and Alvarez.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

The one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

#1350. An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

RNA language models have achieved strong performance across diverse downstream tasks by leveraging large-scale sequence data. However, RNA function is fundamentally shaped by hierarchical structure, making structural information important for pre-training. Existing approaches often depend on noisy annotations or task-specific objectives that can limit generalizability. Here we present structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model trained on 21 million RNA sequence–structure pairs by integrating base-pairing interactions into masked language modelling through a pair-matching operation. We also introduce MUSES, a multi-source ensemble of secondary structures designed to mitigate predictor bias, and a dynamic masking ratio that balances structure-guided and nucleotide-level masking. structRFM learns joint sequence and structure representations as sequence-level, nucleotide-level and pairwise features for broad downstream adaptation. It ranks highly in zero-shot homology classification and establishes new benchmarks for secondary-structure prediction. Its tertiary-structure adaptation, Zfold, consistently improves both three-dimensional predictions and their extracted secondary structures, with performance comparable to AlphaFold31 across CASP15-natural, CASP16 and RNA-Puzzles. structRFM also improves performance on function-prediction tasks and generalizes to newly released RNA families and long non-coding RNAs. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of structure-guided pre-training and highlight multimodal RNA language models for robust structural and functional inference. The complete 21-million-pair dataset, model weights and source code are openly available to support multimodal RNA foundation-model development.

a Ternary simplex visualization of the MUSES performance landscape across weighted combination configurations. Each vertex corresponds to a single standalone method (BPfold, ViennaRNA or CONTRAfold), and interior points represent weighted ensemble models. We normalized weighting coefficients for proportional equivalence and applied linear interpolation over a dense grid to smooth the INF metric distribution. Colour gradients (blue to red) represent INF values, with contour lines for enhanced resolution. This visualization illustrates how ensemble weighting modulates MUSES performance for robust secondary-structure annotation and identifies optimal weight-coefficient regimes with associated trade-offs. b Benchmark evaluation of six established multi-source RNA secondary-structure prediction methods23,24,25,26,34,44,45,79 on the Rfam66,67 and full ArchiveII37 (n = 3, 975 independent RNA sequences) datasets, stratified by three sequence-length categories (≤ 500 nt, 501–1000 nt, > 1000 nt). c Linear fits extrapolating prediction performance for the six methods on both datasets. Lines are linear regression fits, and shaded bands represent 95% confidence intervals. A substantial performance degradation is observed with increasing sequence length, highlighting the current challenge of modelling RNA secondary structures for long RNA sequences.

a Head-to-head comparison of structRFM with other models using ϵRMSD72, TM-score73, GDT-TS74 and INF75. Circle size indicates the absolute difference between the two methods. b Violin plots of RMSD values. For each method in b, n = 8 independent RNA targets for CASP15-natural, n = 13 independent RNA targets for CASP16, and n = 20 independent RNA targets for RNA-Puzzles. The inner box plots show the median (white centre line), 25th and 75th percentiles (lower and upper bounds of the thick line), and minimum and maximum (lower and upper thin whiskers).

The ϵRMSD, TM-score and GDT-TS of tertiary structures, together with the INF of secondary structures extracted from tertiary structures, are annotated. In the secondary-structure diagrams, stems are shown in green, multiple loops in red, interior loops in yellow, hairpin loops in blue, and 5′ and 3′ unpaired regions in orange. In general, structRFM performs better on natural targets than on synthetic targets containing dense long-range interactions, but sometimes fails to predict short local stems (in green), resulting in large multiple loops (in red).

The ϵRMSD, TM-score and GDT-TS of tertiary structures, together with the INF of secondary structures extracted from tertiary structures, are annotated. In the secondary-structure diagrams, stems are shown in green, multiple loops in red, interior loops in yellow, hairpin loops in blue, and 5’ and 3’ unpaired regions in orange. In general, structRFM performs better on viral and aptamer targets but performs worse on multimer and bacterial targets. For targets marked with blue circles, the sequences used for CASP16 prediction differ substantially from those of the PDB ground-truth structures because regions unresolved in the experimental structures were not modelled.

#1348. Scott Parker's baptism of fire: West Ham fight back from three goals down to earn draw at Cardiff in new manager's first match in charge

Published: 18:32 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:18 EDT, 5 November 2026

Scott Parker's West Ham launched a thrilling comeback from three goals down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff in his first game in charge.

Jack Moylan’s first hat-trick in English football had Cardiff in cruise control at half-time and the travelling fans were furious in the away end.

But the Hammers – inspired by captain Jarrod Bowen – fought back in incredible fashion as Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman netted to secure a point for the new boss.

Parker was confirmed as Hammers manager on Wednesday morning – just 24 hours after Nuno Espirito Santo was sacked.

Nuno was axed after a run of poor performances and the club opted to bring in a familiar face, with Parker having made 129 appearances for them as a player between 2007-2011.

It was a tough watch for the former England midfielder initially as Moylan had Cardiff 3-0 ahead inside 39 minutes.

Scott Parker took charge of his first West Ham game after Nuno Espirito Santo's sacking

Max Kilman is seen scoring the dramatic equaliser to make it 3-3 against Cardiff

Moylan scored a hat-trick on his Republic of Ireland debut against Grenada in May, but this was his first club treble since scoring three for Shelbourne in May 2023.

The draw extends Cardiff’s unbeaten home league run to 10 games over the last two seasons, while West Ham occupy the final play-off place in eighth.

Nuno’s 13-month tenure had ended after the Hammers had won just twice in six matches and lost successive home games to Southampton and West Brom.

Taty Castellanos had hinted at better times ahead, forcing Nathan Trott into early action after Bowen’s effort had deflected to him.

But the Hammers were behind after Alex Robertson found Moylan in the 11th minute. Moylan advanced to find the top corner of Mads Hermansen’s net with a ferocious strike from 20 yards.

Hermansen tipped aside Calum Scanlon’s cross and Will Fish headed over as Cardiff probed. There was no reprieve for West Ham when Perry Ng curled a ball over a static defence after 36 minutes.

Moylan cleverly slowed down for Morato to bundle him over, a clear penalty.

Cardiff had missed their last two spot-kicks, but this time Moylan was entrusted with the responsibility and sent Hermansen the wrong way.

Angry Hammers fans responded with cries of ‘you’re not fit to wear the shirt’, and many of them appeared to be making a swift departure three minutes later.

Jarrod Bowen was a key man for the Hammers as they staged a remarkable recovery

Joel Bagan’s corner cleared Fish at the near post, but Moylan came in behind him to head home his sixth goal in five games, and his 10th of the season.

Parker sent on Mohamadou Kante and Joel Piroe for Soungoutou Magassa and Castellanos at half-time and there was instantly more conviction from the Hammers.

Bowen floated a delicious pass through after 58 minutes, and Mukasa lifted the ball over Trott and in off a post.

The deficit was reduced further seven minutes later when Piroe flicked on Bowen’s pass and Engels slid home his first Hammers goal.

Kante nearly toe poked the ball past Trott before Kilman touched home Bowen’s brilliant cross, and West Ham almost won it through substitutes Ezra Mayers and Tomas Soucek.
