#1321. Sarri: ‘Atalanta mental strength important now, Kairat Almaty hidden danger’

Maurizio Sarri warns of the ‘hidden dangers’ Atalanta face in the Conference League against Kairat Almaty, adding that ‘mental strength’ is more important than tactics right now.

It kicks off at the New Balance Arena in Bergamo at 17.45 GMT (18.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game, Milan-Ferencvaros and AZ Alkmaar-Juventus on the Liveblog.

It was always going to be difficult adapting to a new coach with a very different playing style from the previous decade, but it has still been tougher than expected for the team to find a fit with Sarri.

To make matters worse, the injury crisis has ruled out Thomas Kristensen, Gianluca Gaetano, Raoul Bellanova, Franck Kessie, Sead Kolasinac, Isak Hien, Giacomo Raspadori and Odilon Kossounou.

“Kairat changed coach just before the end of their domestic season, so it is a bit of a tactical mystery how they will play,” Sarri told Sky Sport Italia.

“We studied what we could, they only played one game under the new coach, and it was irrelevant to their table. They promoted the Under-19 coach, so we watched a few of the Youth League matches, but we don’t know a lot, other than the characteristics of the individual players.”

Zhora Arutyunyan was indeed promoted as interim coach for the 1-1 draw with Altay Oskemen on October 31, replacing Rafael Urazbakhtin.

“Kairat had some good results, they lost narrowly in the Champions League last season to Inter and in London, so there is nothing easy about this. There are hidden dangers.”

Youth team defender Javison Idele is given his first start for the senior Atalanta team.

“There wasn’t much choice for the line-up, especially considering there is another game coming up on Sunday. The injured players are out, some others looked fatigued and there was no point running risks. We’ll see if we manage to get at least one back for this weekend.”

Atalanta managed just two draws from their last six competitive matches, and on Monday hit a new low with a 3-0 home defeat to relegation strugglers Parma, prompting the squad to be placed into a three-day training retreat.

In the Conference League, they had started with a 3-1 success against Pafos, but then lost 2-0 away to Dutch giants Ajax.

“The first half with Parma was solid, but after the break it became more about character and mental strength than football. We talked about this too,” concluded Sarri.

“These days together helped us to have that discussion, at times we talked about other things too, but I think it was helpful.”

#1320. Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury

This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

Alonso is speedily shifting perceptions of this previously underperforming bunch, the Stamford Bridge culture on and off the pitch already unrecognisable from a few months ago.

It was Chelsea’s trip to Everton last season which facilitated the endgame of Liam Rosenior’s short, but generally hideous reign.

For those who tried to banish memories, it was a darkly comical period when Chelsea’s players were paying their respect to stationary footballs, seemingly finding new ways to stand in front of travelling fans to apologise for meek and rancid performances.

How different the scenes after Pedro Neto’s double on Merseyside – a success built on those old-fashioned and too often underestimated qualities of character and application before the artists had the final say. These are the wins that build connections and trust between players and supporters, especially during the getting-to-know-you period of a managerial tenure. While neutrals mutter about a generally disappointing spectacle, the players and supporters return home clutching three points believing they have fought together in the trenches.

Neto fires past Pickford to double Chelsea's lead! 🔥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/SOJeBP5mq0

It cannot be overlooked how this win owed a debt to the erratic refereeing of Paul Tierney, especially the amnesty he offered to Morgan Rogers on the stroke of half-time.

Already booked, Rogers was fortunate not to receive a second caution for a lunge on James Garner which took the man after the ball. A replica challenge by Everton’s Harrison Armstrong had warranted a yellow card in Tierney’s world just 21 minutes earlier.

The home team’s argument that this was a potential game changer was supported when the England midfielder was inevitably involved in the move which led to Neto breaking through 44 seconds into the second half – a lead Chelsea never looked like surrendering as Everton’s attacking limitations were exposed.

Chelsea break the deadlock inside a minute of the second half! ⚡ Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/E63rtGQnbv

That should not disguise how this is a different Chelsea, contrasting not just with the characterless and rudderless team of last season, but also the defensively flawed version that began this one. Mike Penders deputised for the stricken Martínez – conscious but taken to hospital as a precaution – and was well-protected.

As much as Alonso’s artistry as a midfield maestro is presumed to define him as a coach, one cannot help but believe there are many who underestimate him as a football student. He was never going to return to England clinging to one idea given his previous Premier League experience, and he intuitively knew an away game at Everton was one for foot soldiers.

He signed Jordan Henderson for such a task. Just like his manager, the former Liverpool captain was primed for enemy territory.

Alonso’s anticipation of a fixture in which a battle had to be fought before there was an outbreak of football proved correct, aided by the fussy and generally terrible first-half officiating of Tierney.

Bizarrely, Alonso had as much cause to curse Tierney for the first of several contentious decisions, booking Armstrong for an aggressive but ultimately fair lunging challenge on Josh Acheampong. That enraged the home supporters to inspire Everton to their most dangerous spell, Thierno Barry coming closest to troubling Martínez before half-time.

Although Moisés Caicedo was denied a goal-of-the-season contender when a vicious 20-yard volley struck the crossbar, the scrappy, stop-start flavour of the occasion initially suited the hosts.

Caicedo rattles the woodwork with a stunning effort! 💥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/CSIM9ogtSp

Rogers’s reprieve changed all that. Inexplicably inconsistent as Tierney was, Chelsea exhibited a steel which thrilled Alonso as much as those games when Cole Palmer, Rogers and João Pedro are in full flow.

“They didn’t score, but did a fantastic job for the team,” Alonso pointedly said of his attackers.

Alonso’s name has not echoed so loudly across the Mersey since he played a few miles down the road from Everton’s new home. After several calamitous appointments, those fans can believe their team are in safe hands again.

A good win for Chelsea at Everton, but above all, let’s hope Martinez is back to full health soon.

Moyes accepted that his side had were not good enough.

He told TNT Sports: “We were a little bit unlucky with the goals. It wasn’t good defending, but it takes a couple of deflections before it gets to Neto. It makes it a relatively easy finish for him.

“The second one was a free-kick which obviously ricochets around, so I think there were parts of the game we did OK, but we didn’t offer enough to create enough, to make enough chances. I can’t think of many, so that is probably the biggest indictment.”

He had a minor gripe over a first-half tackle that was reviewed, saying, “I think the Morgan Rogers tackle on Jimmy [Garner] could have been questioned.”

However, given the good start to the season for Everton so far, he does not have too much rancour.

He describes the planned tests as “precautionary” and says, “as far as I know, he left the stadium conscious.”

Neto added more detail to his thoughts on the game.

On his first goal, he explained how Everton’s defensive approach allowed them to react: “We know that they came man-to man. In the second half we adjusted some stuff. We tried to get the best of the man-to-man press and we got away. We got the cross and I could finish well, so really happy.”

He credited his Portugal coach, Jorge Jesus, with his calmness in front of goal, adding: “This comes a little bit from the new coach of the national team that says when you are near to the area you need to pass to the goal, so really happy with that.”

Acheampong sticks a leg out and catches Grealish as he bursts forward, and gets a booking. An early moment of contact in the box between Pedro and Tarkowski is reviewed, and it is waved away.

Moments later, tempers fray as Henderson objects to a foul, I think from Tarkowski, and they all come together for a shoving. Rogers and Tarkowski are booked as the Everton defender barged into the Rogers off the ball.

Everton have had 31% of the ball, but they’re coming back into it. A set piece works the ball to Grealish from Dewsbury-Hall, and he volleys into the ground that Martinez tips away. Everton build patiently from the corner, but Grealish is tackled on the left wing.

A booking for Armstrong for what those of a certain age will consider an aggressive, on-the-edge, but ultimately fair tackle, qualifies as today’s first “the game has gone” moment.

A shot of note. A wild moment. Rohl skids into the box and digs out a shot from inside the box, but it’s hardly magical and it’s easily stopped.

Martinez concedes a corner by holding onto the ball for too long, and Neto gets booked for dissent. An awful corner, and it’s cleared, but Grealish picks the ball and delivers for Barry, who glances his effort straight at Martinez. A decent spell for Everton.

Palmer boots the ball into the air in frustration after a decision goes against him, and he escapes a booking. I mean, it’s hardly a great offence, but now Everton fans will be alert to anything similar that might go against him.

Armstrong then does go into the book for a strong tackle on Acheampong, with both sides up in arms over the decision.

He took the ball, and the man, but while it was fairly meaty, it wasn’t dirty.

Colwill and Barry collide off the ball but there are no afters, Chelsea keep looking.

Neto pulls the ball back for Neto a few moments later, but his low shot is blocked, and Chelsea push forward again.

Corner on the right wing for Everton. Dewsbury-Hall’s cross is cleared at the near post. Grealish sends it back in, but it is overhit and drifts out of play. Chris Bascombe observes the stop-start nature of the game.

Referee Paul Tierney appears to be in one of those moods where if anyone falls over near an opponent, he’ll give a foul. It’s making for a scrappy game, which is suiting Everton.

A shot! Palmer lines up a shot from 25 yards, onto his left foot. It bounces in front of Pickford, who holds well. Pickford has five goals in seven appearances against Everton, so he probably fancies his chances.

Caicedo is crowded out by Dewsbury-Hall, and the Chelsea man almost goes into the book for his efforts. Given his early fouls and arguments, he may be walking on thin ice.

Everton playing like a completely Moyes side. At their best, they are dangerous on the counter and solid at the back. When it goes wrong, the lack of creativity hurts Moyes’ sides, but right now they are holding their own.

Given the jeering for Henderson from the Evertonians, they clearly have not softened their stance on his Anfield past after seeing him tapping the Chelsea badge last weekend. A few Liverpool supporters watching might share their sentiments.

Pedro appears to have taken a clump to the gob, and has a mouthful of tissue or bandage to stem the flow. He remains on the pitch, though.

Grealish plucks a Chelsea crossfield ball out of the air as if he was smoking a cigarette rolled by Dimitar Berbatov as he listened to Ornette Coleman. Sadly after that, his pass out to the right wing went nowhere.

Grealish chases a ball over the top and wins a throw on the left wing. The Everton fans are in decent voice. Mykolenko launches a long throw into the box, but it’s cleared for now.

Grealish and Caiceido get up in each others’ grills, but it settles down.

Chelsea keep the ball for most of the early stages, but Caicedo concedes a foul in midfield.

Chelsea captain Reece James’ surgery could be out for a couple of months, Xabi Alonso explained.

He told the  press: “I wish him the best recovery. We won’t set timelines, but we expect him to be out for several weeks. It’s not going to be short. Whether it’s before or after Christmas then time will tell. It needs to be done properly.”

He is looking to vice captains Moises Caceido and Levi Colwill to step up in his absence, explaining: “You can be a captain without an armband, for sure. Leadership is important and that’s why we have this group, not just on matchday.”

James remains vital to Chelsea at their best, and while his minutes have been managed, it’s a huge disappointment to see him need to go under the knife once more.

In his press conference ahead of the weekend, Everton boss David Moyes was not too concerned by his relatively small squad.He said:  “Leicester City won the league with not too many players. We have not got too many players. I am not saying we’re going to win the league, but we want to try to challenge and be around the top teams.”

That might be made harder by the news that the Friedkin Group are already looking to sell the club after only a couple of years in charge. Moyes is a rare thing, a manager who keeps improving despite setbacks, and his second spell has been fairly solid so far.

Moyes is aware that Chelsea pose a threat up front, adding: “Their attacking line is incredibly exciting. I also think they have got some super defenders as well, but they are playing quite an expansive game, which on its day can lead to goals and on another day it can lead to defeats.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Everton vs Chelsea.

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend looking to harness the momentum of their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth before the international break. That Stamford Bridge masterclass ended a frustrating three-match winless streak and was built upon braces from Joao Pedro and Jordan Henderson, alongside another strike from summer signing Morgan Rogers.

Yet the true catalyst for the resurgence was the return of Moises Caicedo. Having shaken off the calf problem that hindered his early-season involvement, the midfielder anchored the side’s win. While defensive vulnerabilities persist - extending an unwanted run of league matches without a clean sheet back to January - the victory offered clear signs of progress under their head coach, Xabi Alonso.

Next up is a notoriously difficult trip to Merseyside to face Everton in Saturday’s lunchtime fixture. Historically, Everton have proven to be a formidable stumbling block for the capital club, particularly on home turf. Everton enter the weekend unbeaten in eight of their last nine home encounters against Chelsea, a stretch that has seen the Londoners fail to score on seven visits and suffer six defeats, including a chastening 3-0 reverse last term that spelt the end for Liam Rosenior.

David Moyes will demand a sharper defensive showing from his side this time around, following a frustrating 2-2 draw with Hull City where a 2-1 lead slipped away. Even so, Everton’s broader defensive record at home offers encouragement, having kept clean sheets in two of their opening three league fixtures at their base.

With both teams eager to build consistency, Saturday’s clash pits Chelsea’s newly found attacking spark against an opponent that traditionally relishes this fixture.

#1318. Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome1. Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized, owing to limited identification of host receptors2, which hinders pathogenesis research and therapeutic development. Here, using proximity biotin labelling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR–Cas9 validation, we identify nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor. Ectopic expression of nectin-4 conferred susceptibility to RuV in non-permissive cells, whereas blocking or genetic ablation of nectin-4 reduced infection, results that demonstrate that nectin-4 is a major entry factor. Mechanistically, nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoprotein heterodimer and facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment to cellular lipids. In polarized airway epithelial models, nectin-4 mediates basolateral entry of RuV and supports apical progeny release, a finding that provides a molecular mechanism for respiratory transmission. In placental models, nectin-4 is highly expressed on syncytiotrophoblasts and facilitates infection at the maternal–fetal interface, although additional nectin-4-independent pathways contribute to infection of other trophoblast populations. Together, these data establish nectin-4 as a key factor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of RuV and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of rubella and related diseases.

#1317. Huge for Iraola: Liverpool About to Officially Agree Terms With Trey Nyoni

Liverpool appear to have hit a sticky patch under Andoni Iraola following a largely positive start to the season under the Spaniard.

Liverpool were unbeaten in all competitions heading into the first international break, but their first match after ended in a 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City.

The Reds did bounce back from that with five consecutive wins, including a penalty shootout victory against Chelsea in the EFL Cup, but they have since lost twice to Arsenal and then Fenerbahce in the Champions League.

The form of the likes of Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola is still up and down despite their £100m-plus fees, while the defence continues to be a cause for concern for the former Bournemouth boss.

Wednesday night's 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce was the third consecutive Champions League game that they had conceded three goals in, and it ended their 100% record in the competition.

Clearly an improvement is needed on the training ground from a defensive point of view, while Iraola still needs to work out how exactly to get the best out of Wirtz and Barcola, based on what we've seen from the big-money duo this term.

One area the 44-year-old might be happier is in midfield, with Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai, Ryan Gravenberch and Trey Nyoni pushing for two starting spots in the XI.

After signing new long-term contracts earlier in 2026, you may have expected Szoboszlai and Gravenberch to be the first-choice partnership in Liverpool's engine room, but instead it is the other two who have probably shone most under Iraola to date.

Nyoni in the Champions League this season

Mac Allister looks to be the most motivated of the more senior central midfielders even though the club currently have no plans to offer the Argentina international a new contract, according to GIVEMESPORT sources.

The jury is out on the performances of both Szoboszlai and Gravenberch this term, including when the Reds' midfield instantly lost control when the duo replaced Nyoni and James McConnell in the 3-1 EFL Cup win against Tottenham.

Nyoni has impressed so much that he is now on the verge of signing a contract extension at Anfield.

Nyoni has now made 32 first-team appearances for Liverpool, so while his involvement this term under Iraola shouldn't be a surprise, what is a surprise is the fact that he is getting to the stage where he is making himself an automatic starter because of the quality he is showing.

The midfielder only turned 19 years of age in June, but he looks like he has been playing for the Reds for years and looks completely fearless and composed every time he steps onto the pitch for the Merseysiders.

Nyoni is providing a midfield solidity that isn't there when Gravenberch and Szoboszlai play together, and Wirtz tends to thrive more when the teenager is on the pitch and his defensive work rate is reduced as a result.

The youngster has been especially outstanding for the Reds in the Champions League this term, starting their previous three games in the competition.

While he is primarily a defensively-minded player, he even popped up with a goal against Fenerbahce on Wednesday night.

OptaJoe posted on Thursday morning that the teenager has also completed 92% of his passes under high intensity in Europe's elite club competition, which is the highest accuracy of any midfielder who has attempted 100 passes or more.

It actually puts Nyoni ahead of second-placed Pedri (91%), who is considered one of the best young central midfielders in the world after the impact he has made for Barcelona.

It's still early days in the midfielder's career, but the level he is playing at this season suggests Liverpool have a generational talent on their hands.

If they get the contract renewal over the line in the coming days and weeks, it can only be a big boost for Iraola, who clearly loves the 19-year-old.

Liverpool must permanently change Dominik Szoboszlai's position as he's holding them back in his current role.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#1316. Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card

Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

For Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews said. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”

Brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very important points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

The loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa said: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. One of the advantages of Iraola’s Anfield appointment was his Premier League experience with Bournemouth. The Basque well knows the division and has plenty of positive memories from which to borrow.

However, there will also be some scar tissue, and that certainly is the case with Brentford. Iraola never beat the Bees in seven attempts (five draws, two defeats), a run which included a 4-1 thrashing at the Gtech Community Stadium in his final season at Bournemouth.

But Maresca has changed half of his team from the line-up defeated by Paris St-Germain in the week. Jeremy Doku and City’s first-choice centre-backs are the others to keep their place. The rest are drafted in to face Ipswich, with Matheus Nunes, Nico O’Reilly, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Iliman Ndiaye and Mateo Kovačić are drafted in.

There is also a place for Phil Foden after serving his three-match ban for getting dismissed in the Manchester derby.

Keith Andrews has established a clearly defined, direct style of play which speaks to Brentford’s strengths. His side are third in the Premier League for percentage of passes forward (39.2 per cent) and, coupled with the second-most high turnovers which end in a goal, Brentford have thrived off passages of organised chaos.

To play this way requires quality when you do have the ball, and full-backs Keane Lewis-Potter and Michael Kayode deserve particular praise. They have contributed materially to Brentford’s attacks, helping their side to league-high successful crosses (26) and expected goals from set-pieces (4.03).

Manchester City’s claim to have “irrefutable evidence” that will overturn their guilty verdict on appeal is based on a trove of emails, letters and bank statements.

A re-examination of Abu Dhabi government documents, receipts and testimony from 24 witnesses – all of which the club believe were wrongly dismissed at the original hearing – will be central in attempts to force a full or partial acquittal or retrial, according to people familiar with the case.

City’s legal team will attempt to demonstrate “fundamental errors” in tests applied by an independent commission to the Premier League’s case that commercial revenue was artificially inflated by £920m. Sources with understanding of City’s case have told Telegraph Sport the club are bullish about their appeal, based on:

Shahid Khan, Fulham’s owner, insists that his team are on a “positive path” despite remaining winless in the Premier League after six matches.

In his programme notes, he wrote: “I want to reflect on our recent form. Prior to the international break, we were trending upward… That momentum carried us through most of Saturday’s match at Ipswich Town, but we all know how that ended. The result was devastating for all of us, and I won’t pretend otherwise.

“And yet, I am reminded of the positive path we have been on and the genuine potential of this team. Our squad is strong, while still coming together. We have been in every match, missing only the opportunities we’ve had to complete the task. I believe those opportunities will soon be seized.”

This feels like an extremely treacherous trip for Liverpool and for Andoni Iraola, who has a poor record against Brentford. With Bournemouth, he did not win any of his six matches against today’s opponents.

The good news for Liverpool is that Alexander Isak and Dominik Szoboszlai are fit enough to start the game, and that Brentford top scorer Kevin Schade is not. Schade is on the bench after picking up a shoulder injury against Aston Villa last weekend.

Barcola opened his Liverpool account on Wednesday and he will look to continue his goal-scoring form at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Speaking of the France winger, head coach Andoni Iraola said: “I think it’s still very early, especially for him who hasn’t played any minutes in pre-season, he’s kind of been doing pre-season in the first games with us almost [in] official games.

“It’s remarkable because to score three goals in a Champions League game is … not a lot of players can say they have done it.

“It’s something nice for him but I think the best thing is we can feel him, he seems with confidence on the ball [away] from the goals, straight away you could feel he was confident going in one-to-one situations, attacking the spaces and [those] are his strengths.”

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the 3pm kick-offs. Manchester City burst the Anfield bubble last weekend but were defeated by Paris St-Germain in a Champions League thriller on Wednesday, and Enzo Maresca will have to manage his leading cast members’ workload. Before Ipswich Town’s visit to the Etihad he floated the idea of resting some of his players at some point.

“We are thinking about this not just with Erling [Haaland] because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams,” Maresca said in his pre-match press conference.”

“Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernández], Marc [Guéhi], Erling, Rúben [Dias] – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest.”

Ipswich’s spirited start to the season was characterised by a stunning late turnaround against Fulham last weekend. Gary O’Neil’s side have accrued three wins in their first six top-flight matches for the first time since 1993 and may consider today’s match as something of a free hit.

Elsewhere, Liverpool’s confidence-building midweek win in Austria was underlined by Bradley Barcola’s first, second and third goals for the club. It was exactly what the France winger needed, and with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo emerging as doubts for this afternoon’s trip to Brentford, the attacking burden may fall on Barcola and Florian Wirtz’s shoulders once more.

Breaking down fourth-placed Brentford, who are one of only three teams to remain undefeated this season, will be a tall task. Keith Andrews’ stock has never been higher, but the same cannot be said for Álvaro Arbeloa, whose winless Fulham are bottom of the league.

Pressure was already mounting before Fulham’s three-game run against the promoted teams, and the late collapse at Portman Road will not have helped the Spaniard’s cause. Defeat by Hull City will not be seen kindly by the club’s hierarchy.

#1315. Official: Mancini names 31-man Italy squad for France and Belgium

Roberto Mancini has named an Italy national team squad of 31 players for the upcoming Nations League fixtures against France and Belgium in November, including several fresh faces in Alphadjo Cisse, Simone Lontani and Riccardo Cassano.

Italy will be in action against France in San Siro next Thursday, November 12, and away against Belgium on Sunday, November 15.

As things stand, Italy sit in second place in their Nations League group on seven points after four matches. France lead the way on 10, Belgium are in third on six and Turkiye are bottom on zero.

After naming a squad of 34 players for his first camp back in charge of the Italy national team last month, Mancini has named a roster of 31 players this time around, handing call-ups to several uncapped players including Cisse, Lontani, Cassano, Mattia Liberali and Luca Koleosho.

There is also a call-up for Honest Ahanor, who earned his first two caps under Silvio Baldini in a pair of international friendlies back in June, but has not yet earned his first cap in a competitive fixture. He was selected in September, but did not feature and was then allowed to return to the Italy U21 side to help them qualify for the upcoming European Championships.

There is also a return to the Italy squad for Marco Palestra, who has recently made his first Premier League appearances for Chelsea after picking up an injury just before the season began.

There are no major surprises in terms of absentees: The regular core of Gianluigi Donnarumma, Alessandro Bastoni, Riccardo Calafiori, Federico Dimarco, Nicolo Barella, Sandro Tonali and Pio Esposito have all been included.

There is no Giovanni Di Lorenzo, who was forced off injured at half-time of Napoli’s recent 2-0 defeat against Juventus.

Goalkeepers: Marco Carnesecchi (Atalanta), Gianluigi Donnarumma (Man City), Guglielmo Vicario (Juventus).

Defenders: Honest Ahanor (Crystal Palace), Alessandro Bastoni (Inter), Riccardo Calafiori (Arsenal), Federico Dimarco (Inter), Daniele Ghilardi (Roma), Michael Kayode (Brentford), Gianluca Mancini (Roma), Marco Palestra (Chelesa), Giorgio Scalvini (Atalanta).

Midfielders: Nicolò Barella (Inter), Riccardo Cassano (Como), Issa Doumbia (Sporting CP), Nicolò Fagioli (Fiorentina), Davide Frattesi (Lazio), Simone Lontani (Parma), Niccolò Pisilli (Roma), Samuele Ricci (Como), Alessandro Romano (Cagliari), Sandro Tonali (Tottenham).

Attackers: Nicolò Cambiaghi (Bologna), Alphadjo Cisse (Milan), Francesco Pio Esposito (Inter), Sebastiano Esposito (Sassuolo), Luca Koleosho (Paris FC), Mattia Liberali (Como), Gianluca Scamacca (Atalanta), Antonio Vergara (Napoli), Nicolo Zaniolo (Udinese).

📋💙 La lista dei 31 convocati del Ct Roberto #Mancini per le prossime sfide di Nations League contro Francia e Belgio#Nazionale 🇮🇹 #Azzurri #VivoAzzurro pic.twitter.com/yFgZYqDwlR

#1314. Now will the FA put their money where their mouth is? England chiefs and UEFA must decide whether to back rival Japanese bid to FIFA president Gianni Infantino after slamming World Cup controversial sell-off plan

Published: 08:23 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 11:00 EDT, 5 November 2026

The FA and UEFA face a dilemma over whether to support a bid to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency after honorary Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima announced his decision to stand.

Alongside the FA, UEFA have spearheaded opposition to Infantino following the collapse of his botched deal to sell stakes in the World Cup.

However, despite declaring Infantino 'has lost the confidence of UEFA' and threatening to boycott the World Cup, the European governing body have so far failed to come up with a candidate to challenge him at the March election in Rabat.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin decided against a run for the FIFA presidency, opting instead to focus on securing another term at the top of European football.

At a meeting of the FA Council last month FA chair Debbie Hewitt demanded answers over the World Cup sell-off plan - and decision to suspend the ban of US striker Folarin Balogun after pressure from Donald Trump. She said: 'The man has to answer those questions, and if he doesn't answer those questions, no, he's not fit to be FIFA president, and that was what was shared in the meeting.'

But there is a growing feeling that a European candidate would struggle to secure sufficient support from the rest of the world, while Infantino believes he already has enough votes to secure re-election, making it difficult to find a credible challenger.

Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima has announced a decision to stand for FIFA presidency

Tashima will run against the controversial current president Gianni Infantino (left)

That said, FIFA Council member and Japanese FA bigwig Tashima could split the Asian vote and is well respected in Europe.

With Tashima - the first candidate to secure the backing of a national association - declaring his intention to run, pressure is now mounting on the FA and UEFA to either support his bid or put forward a candidate of their own, having called for Infantino to step down.

It follows former Tottenham and Switzerland footballer Ramon Vega making a public leadership bid on Wednesday, though it is unclear whether he could obtain the backing of enough national associations.

Candidates require the support of five football associations to run for the presidency and must pass eligibility checks by November 18.

Tashima is the first candidate with a realistic chance to announce an intention to run before the November 18 deadline, where the support of five national associations is required.

Speaking to Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon, Tashima said: ‘I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association.

‘It’s not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.’

#1313. Southampton Must Axe Mubama in January With Nmecha the Perfect Replacement

With gameweek 14 now complete in the Championship, Southampton know that they would be top of the table were it not for their four-point deduction.

Southampton have started the 2026-27 season where they left off last term, and while they look formidable at home, Tonda Eckert will know that there is an improvement to be made on the road with both of their league defeats coming away at Watford and Wrexham.

Only six points separates top-of-the-table Middlesbrough and 10th-placed Portsmouth, in what looks set to be another exciting campaign in England's second tier, where teams know that an eighth-place finish is now enough to guarantee a spot in the playoff positions.

On paper, Saints don't look to have too many weaknesses given they have the joint-best goal difference (15) in the league alongside West Ham, with only the Hammers and Boro scoring more than their total of 29.

Meanwhile, only Birmingham City have conceded fewer goals than their 14, with their defensive record improving significantly since the last international break.

The south coast outfit clearly have one of the strongest first-choice starting XIs in the division, but there are concerns about the strength in depth behind them in certain positions.

Defensively they largely look well covered, although there are question marks over the back-up to James Bree, while they are well stocked in central midfield, especially when all four of James Ward-Prowse, Caspar Jander, Flynn Downes and Cameron Bragg are fit.

The front four, when fit, picks itself, in Leo Scienza, Finn Azaz, Kuryu Matsuki and Cyle Larin, but the latter has missed the club's previous three matches through injury.

Southampton have dealt well without their top goalscorer with eight goals during that period, but there is an increasing feeling that Divin Mubama isn't at the level required when Larin is absent.

Divin Mubama for Southampton (Championship)

Eckert handed the Manchester City loanee is his first league start of the campaign in Tuesday's 1-1 draw with West Bromwich Albion, but he just isn't making the same impact that Larin, and more recently Lewis Dobbin, have in the centre-forward position.

Saints' German manager clearly doesn't rate him too highly either given most of his appearances have come as a late substitute, playing just 205 Championship minutes in total.

One of the reasons Southampton were so strong in the first half of 2026 is that Eckert was often bringing the likes of Shea Charles and Ross Stewart off the bench, but there is a feeling that their depth isn't quite as strong this time around.

Mubama isn't showing he is anywhere near the quality that Stewart was last term, and Saints need to put that right in the January transfer window.

The young striker surely won't be happy with his lack of minutes, and neither will Manchester City as they look for him to develop, so the best course of action unless things improve in the next two months would be to terminate the loan early and bring in someone who can have a bigger influence on the promotion push.

Sporting director Johannes Spors may have already identified the perfect replacement in Leeds United's Lukas Nmecha, with TEAMtalk reporting last month that the club is looking at a move for the seven-cap Germany international.

Nmecha joined Leeds on a free transfer in the summer of 2025, but with his contract due to expire at the end of this season, there is every chance he could be moving for nothing again.

The 27-year-old has seen his playing time in the Premier League this season limited, despite the fact he has scored seven goals in 47 outings for the Yorkshire outfit, having started just 10 top flight games.

Nmecha wants to play regularly and he will have a point to prove at his next club. The fact that he has played for Germany, and was a prolific scorer for Wolfsburg in the Bundesliga previously, makes him an attractive option for a club like Southampton, who want to be a Premier League club next term.

Convincing the German to play second tier football for six months could be a challenge, but if he can help them achieve promotion, then he could be a top-flight player again anyway.

He's making no impact in a Southampton shirt under Tonda Eckert

#1312. Portuguese Media React to Cristiano Ronaldo's International Retirement

At the ripe old age of 41, Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football with Portugal. The iconic forward departs having scored a record 146 goals in 234 caps, most notably winning Euro 2016.

In an emotional farewell message, he said: "To the Portuguese people, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and taking it with me to stadiums all over the world. Today the moment has come to hand it over to the future. It wasn't an easy decision, because there are decisions that aren't made only with the head. They are also made with the heart."

Of course, Ronaldo departs as one of the greatest football players of all time, but he also leaves under a bit of a cloud. His final appearances with the national team before making the decision to retire were rather controversial. Indeed, the Al-Nassr striker walked away from the camp after falling out with manager Jorge Jesus over game time.

Many have felt Ronaldo should have retired years ago, and that he was actually holding the team back due to his diminishing quality. With that in mind, it's interesting to see how those in Portugal have reacted to the big news.

Portuguese boss Jesus has naturally given his thoughts on Ronaldo's retirement. He distanced himself from the decision and praised the player's career, stating:

"This is all his decision. We already had the opportunity to talk about this before the first call-up. I asked him to stay, to stay with me because I needed him to be by my side, but I have to accept his decision"

Jesus added: "He is a world reference, a reference for Portugal, a reference for the National Team. He is a player who, throughout these years, has given a lot to the National Team. He is a symbol for Portuguese youth. Most of his fans are young. I had the opportunity to share the experience of working with him for a year at Al Nassr . Therefore, he will always be a reference for our National Team, for our people, for our history."

With Ronaldo's falling out with Jesus in mind, media outlet O Jogo compared the player's exit to Lionel Messi, noting how the Argentine left international football in much happier circumstances: "Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi marked an era in world football, starring in one of the greatest rivalries in the history of the sport for about two decades. However, the end of their respective international careers is proving to be very different: while the Argentinian had a farewell in a festive and celebratory atmosphere, the Portuguese ended his connection with the National Team without fans anticipating that they would never see him again in the national jersey."

Duarte Gomes, the former referee and former technical director of refereeing at the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF), called it a 'shame' that things ended on such bad terms, noting:

"Cristiano Ronaldo will always be a unique figure in the history of Portuguese and world football. His legacy, his career, and everything he offered to the country deserved a different ending. Hardly anyone could have imagined that such an extraordinary connection could end like this. Not even him.

"What saddens me most is not the decision – inevitable in the short term – but the certainty that it should never have happened this way. This outcome is the culmination of a succession of thoughtless, avoidable, and poorly managed episodes, where a glaring inability of everyone – I repeat, everyone – to find a different solution stood out. Regardless of the underlying reasons that may have guided some and others (now irrelevant), one conclusion seems clear to me: somewhere in the process, an adult was missing from the room. A shame."

It's worth noting that the FPF are now planning a final game for Ronaldo to celebrate his career, as they 'refuse to let this farewell take place without due tribute.'

For the most part, however, media outlets across the country were keen to celebrate Ronaldo's special career, one of the most decorated in football history. A Bola, for example, spoke in fond terms of the departing legend, writing:

"Cristiano Ronaldo's farewell to the National Team marks the end of the most golden and impactful era in the history of Portuguese football. Twenty-three years of pure devotion, impossible goals, unprecedented titles, and global records transformed Portugal's status in the world. From his hopeful debut in Chaves in 2003 to his abrupt retirement in Copenhagen, the eternal captain bids farewell with the weight of legend."

Speaking to A Bola in a separate article, former Portugal manager Luiz Felipe Scolari – who gave Ronaldo his international debut in 2003 – insisted that this was the right moment to step away from the national team. He said: "Ronaldo, you did well. You're calm, you made the right decision," before adding: "You were one of the athletes that Portugal will never forget. And I, as your friend and as someone who admires you, will never forget you either, for everything you did with me and with your teammates."

Adding to that, as quoted in O Jogo, former Portugal and Manchester United teammate Nani said: "Congratulations, brother, on this beautiful journey! You inspired us all and made us believe that, as Portuguese people, we could be the best in the world. You made us feel proud of ourselves, as a people and as a team."

"You are and will always be a role model for all of us who follow you and who have shared wonderful moments with you, both on and off the field. The national team is the pinnacle of our careers, and I am incredibly proud to have been a part of your story. For me, you are the best of all time, not only for the player you were and everything you gave to our national team, but also for what you represented to all of us. Even when we often disagreed, we were always growing, improving, and learning. And we owe that to you as well. For all of this, I can only say: thank you very much, Captain! What you did for Portugal and for all of us will never be forgotten."

#1311. Europa League line-ups: AZ Alkmaar vs. Juventus

Both Koopmeiners brothers start in Thrusday evening’s Europa League clash between AZ Alkmaar and Juventus, as Luciano Spalletti keeps his attacking trident of Randal Kolo Muani, Nick Woltemade and Kerim Alajbegovic.

You can follow the action as it unfolds on the Football Italia Liveblog.

The Bianconeri are unbeaten after three matches of the Europa League season, having defeated NEC 5-0 in the first round of league phase fixtures, 2-1 away against Celta Vigo in the second and having drawn 2-2 with Rennes last time out.

Their form domestically has brought more ups and downs, with five wins, two draws, three defeats and a seventh-place ranking on their record after 10 games of the Serie A campaign. The Old Lady head into tonight’s game off the back of a 2-0 win over struggling Napoli in the league over the weekend.

AZ are one point worse off than Juventus in the Europa League after three matches, with two wins (against Hapoel Beer-Sheva and Ararat-Armenia) and one defeat (against Sunderland) thus far. They are hoping to get back to winning ways after consecutive defeats against Twente and Ajax in the Eredivisie over the last two weeks.

Injuries continue to be an issue for Juventus, with Kenan Yildiz, Nico Gonzalez, Francisco Conceicao, Khephren Thuram, Manuel Locatelli, Zeki Celik and Kamil Grabara all unavailable for tonight’s tie. Weston McKennie was the latest player to be added to the Bianconeri injury list.

Hosts AZ are without Jeroen Zoet, Jizz Hornkamp, Wouter Goes and Stije Resik. Kees Smit is in the squad for the first time since September.

Tonight’s game brings a reunion of the Koopmeiners brothers, who have both been included in the starting line-ups. Like his brother, Juventus’s Teun Koopmeiners also came through the AZ Alkmaar academy before joining Atalanta in 2021.

Spalletti has stuck with Kolo Muani at centre-forward and he will be joined by Woltemade and Alajbegovic in the Juve attack.

AZ Alkmaar: De Busser; Kasius, Goes, Schouten, M de Wit; P.Koopmeiners, Kwakman; Stengs, Byskov, Daal; Meerdink.

Juventus: Vicario; Gatti, Lucumi Kelly; Kalulu, Sarr, T.Koopmeiners, Cambiaso; Alajbegovic; Woltemade, Kolo Muani

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1310. Newcastle Star Causes Chaos After Bow and Arrow Incident

A current player on the books of Newcastle United has caused chaos in England after being spotted with a bow and arrow. The Premier League star in question is defender Amar Dedic.

The Bosnian international signed for the Magpies in the summer from Benfica in a deal worth just under £30m. The right-back was consequently reunited with Matthias Jaissle, his former coach at both FC Liefering and RB Salzburg.

Dedic has been a key player for his new side as well, with six starts in the league to his name from the opening nine games, producing two assists in that time. Newcastle, however, will be concerned to learn the defender's car was recently at the centre of a major police operation this week.

Scholes specifically chose one Arsenal player ahead of Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

As reported by the Daily Mail, Dedic sparked police alarm on Wednesday after being spotted carrying a bow and arrows in Northumberland. A concerned member of the public reported the Newcastle defender and a friend after they were seen with the weapon near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

It's said that 'at least six patrol cars' were then involved in the search for the footballer, as they were dispatched to the area in Harlow Hill. Not all the police cars were marked, but it's understood that some were armed response units.

Dedic and his companion were finally intercepted around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate. Sources described a dramatic swoop on Dedic's vehicle before officers searched the car and seized a bow and arrows, with the 24-year-old questioned about his activities.

Adding to the drama, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic. It is said that the pair were simply in the area by chance and stopped to offer assistance.

After speaking to the two men, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public, with police subsequently stating that the equipment was believed to have been intended for recreational use. Dedic is said to have fired some arrows while in the countryside, although it remains unclear what he was aiming at. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in the UK.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson has now shared a statement on the matter. It explained that enquiries remain ongoing into the incident:

"Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

"Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing."

The Daily Mail report also claimed that Dedic will not face disciplinary action from Newcastle over the incident. That said, there is the internal feeling within the club that the player was naive to believe he could walk around the countryside carrying a bow and arrow.

The Bosnian is expected to be available for Saturday's Premier League trip to Fulham.

#1309. The neural basis of flavour–nutrient learning

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Animals learn about the external world in part through interoceptive signals1,2. For example, the nutrient content of food is first estimated in the mouth, in the form of flavour, and then it is measured again through slower signals from the gut. How these signals from the mouth and gut are integrated to drive learning is unclear. Here we identify a dopamine (DA) pathway that enables learning about the nutrient content of food. We show that DA neurons in the ventral tegmental area are necessary for associating nutrients with flavours, and that post-ingestive nutrients trigger DA release selectively in a small region of the anterior basolateral amygdala (BLA) but not in canonical DA targets in striatum. This nutrient-triggered DA release occurs preferentially in the left BLA in mice, and this same structure is preferentially activated by post-ingestive nutrients in humans. We identify the gut sensors that are responsible for nutrient-triggered DA release; show that they activate BLA-projecting DA neurons defined by expression of cholecystokinin; and demonstrate that stimulation of DA axon terminals in the anterior BLA drives flavour–nutrient learning but not other aspects of feeding behaviour. Two-photon imaging of neurons in the left anterior BLA reveals that they integrate gustatory and post-ingestive cues, and silencing these neurons prevents flavour–nutrient learning. These findings establish a neural basis for how animals learn about the nutrient content of their food.

Legends and additional references for Supplementary Tables 1–6.

Behaviour statistics. Summary information for all behavioural tests for each manipulation. Values are reported to 1 decimal place. Number of animals is reported as n. P values are reported for all statistical tests, and are shown in bold if below standard significance level (α = 0.05). In cases in which a Benjamini–Hochberg correction was made for multiple comparisons, an adjusted P value (p′) is shown (where p′ = P × m/i, where i is rank and m is number of cohorts tested; Methods). X′ corresponds to the normalized value of X. For self-stimulation, ‘presses’ means the number of inactive lever presses has been subtracted from the number of active lever presses. In flavour conditioning experiments in which mice began the test with >90% preference for one flavour, statistics are also provided (in parentheses) with these mice excluded. Permutation (perm.) tests use an exact test (or 100,000 iterations if n > 9) and are unpaired, unless otherwise mentioned (note: this means the lowest calculable P value is 1 × 10−5).

Dopamine imaging statistics. Summary information for all recordings of dopamine release in each brain region. Values are reported to 2 decimal places. Number of animals is reported as n. P values are reported for all statistical tests, and are shown in bold if below standard significance level (α = 0.05). X′ corresponds to the normalized value of X. For photometry traces, dF′/F′ means the dF/F values seen during sham infusion have been subtracted. For rise times, s′ means that the time is relative to approximate entry of liquid into the stomach. For fall times, s′ means that the time is relative to the end of the infusion. For peak times during licking, s′ means that the time is relative to the start of the first licking bout. The baseline is defined as the first 10 min of the recording for GI and post-GI measurements, or 0–20 s before the start of the first licking bout for oral measurements. Permutation tests use an exact test (or 100,000 iterations if n >9) and are unpaired, unless otherwise mentioned (note that this means the lowest calculable P value is 1 × 10−5).

Single-cell imaging statistics. Summary information for all 1- and 2-photon miniscope recordings. Values are reported to 2 decimal places. The number (n) of animals and number of cells are reported separately. P values are reported for all statistical tests, and are shown in bold if below standard significance level (α = 0.05). X′ corresponds to the normalized value of X. For rise times, s′ means that the time is relative to either the onset of the licking bout or to the approximate entry of liquid into the stomach. Population-weighted activity (pop-z) is calculated for a group of neurons (for example, activated or inhibited neurons) by multiplying activity by the fraction of neurons belonging to that group. Linear-mixed models (LME) treat mouse differences as both a fixed random effect and covariate (Methods). The relative contribution of mouse differences to total variance is reported by ICCs. Note that, for PCA, the number of PCs is equal to the number of cells. Permutation tests use an exact test (or 100,000 iterations if n > 9) and are unpaired, unless otherwise mentioned (note that this means that the lowest calculable P value for those tests is 1 × 10−5).

fMRI imaging statistics (n = 38). Activity from left and right BLA clusters binned every 2 min (20 min total), as shown in Extended Data Figs. 10f and 11n. For PET statistics, see ref. 56. Each of the ten time bins after glucose intake was contrasted against the baseline (2 min before glucose intake), representing the change in brain activity after glucose intake relative to the baseline. The contrast for the first effect was [ones(1,10)], and for the following contrasts [1], corresponding to the different time bins. The significance threshold was P < 0.05, FWE-corrected for multiple comparisons at the voxel level within the left or right BLA mask, respectively, with initial peak-level threshold set to P < 0.05 uncorrected.

Pseudorabies statistics. Regional labelling (load) was normalized to VTA load to control for injection efficiency. From the 1,328 annotated CCFv3 regions, only grey-matter areas were retained (372 total), with cortical layers collapsed into single structures. Regions smaller than 100 × 100 × 100 pixels were excluded to remove small nuclei with high variance from few labelled cells, yielding 131 analysed regions.

Brain connectivity tables. Connectivity matrices were generated manually, with each pair given a number indicating bidirectional projection strength from 0 (no known direct connection) to 5 (strongest projection known from this area). The connectivity strength between an area and itself was assigned a value of 5. For deciding what strength to assign a projection, large databases like the Allan Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas (ref. 1 of the Supplementary References) were preferred, supplemented by additional sources comprising reviews and anatomical tracing studies (refs. 2–32 of the Supplementary References).

#1308. Tottenham Are Officially The Second Most Dominant Premier League Team

How quickly things can change in the football world.

Just three-and-a-half weeks ago, Tottenham were rock bottom of the Premier League table and without a win to their name, with pressure building on Roberto De Zerbi's shoulders after he had pulled off the great escape last season to guide the Lilywhites to safety in the Premier League.

Fast forward to now, however, and everything is looking rosy for Spurs. They have enjoyed three straight victories to move into the top half of the table and, playing early on Saturday, they could move as high as fifth ahead of the other matches taking place.

De Zerbi splashed the cash in the summer transfer window to put his imprint on the squad he inherited from Thomas Frank and Igor Tudor, spending more than £300million, with that figure to rise to the £400million mark when Omar Marmoush's loan move is made permanent next summer.

It took a while for the players to gel, which is hardly surprising, given ten new faces arrived at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and to get used to De Zerbi's style of football. But things appear to have clicked now, as evidenced by those wins against Coventry City, Chelsea and Crystal Palace.

De Zerbi's philosophy is based around high intensity, possession-based football. The Italian expects his teams to play out from the back, through a ball-playing goalkeeper and centre-backs, playing through a midfield duo and into wingers and a No.10 behind a main striker.

Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke have been crucial to this strategy, with the duo of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes - both new arrivals in the summer - ahead of them key in the midfield double pivot too.

De Zerbi, who ranks highly among current Premier League managers, was described by Pep Guardiola as "one of the most influential managers in the last 20 years" when he was at Brighton in 2023, and it has become clear that his influence is steadily growing on Tottenham too.

Spurs had 34 shots against Palace on Saturday, the most they have had in a match in the Premier League since 2016. It is a far cry from the shot-shy outfit of the last 12 months.

Heatmap graphs from before Spurs moved up the table suggested the side were on the right track unde the Italian, without picking up results, with some suggestions that they were dominating games just like top two Manchester City and Arsenal, despite being in the bottom three.

And, now the players are starting to click, that has proven to be true.

Tottenham are second in the table when it comes to possession so far this season, with only Manchester City averaging more in their nine games of the season.

It is no surprise to know that a De Zerbi team likes to have the ball, but it is perhaps somewhat surprising that Spurs are already the second most dominant team in the Premier League when it comes to having the ball, particularly given how they started the season.

What they have done in the last three matches is found a way to win, to turn their dominance into goals and subsequently three points. If they continue to do that, they could become a force to be reckoned with in the top flight, particularly without the sitraction of European football.

Despite signing a new five-year contract at Tottenham in the summer, he is subject to strong transfer interest from Barcelona

#1307. Mancini names 17-year-old Cassano in latest Italy squad before first club appearance

Roberto Mancini has recently confirmed a squad of 31 players for Italy’s upcoming Nations League fixtures against France and Belgium, and to much surprise, has included 17-year-old Como midfielder Riccardo Cassano, who has not yet made a competitive appearance at club level.

Italy will be in action against France in San Siro next Thursday, November 12, and away against Belgium on Sunday, November 15.

As things stand, Italy sit in second place in their Nations League group on seven points after four matches. France lead the way on 10, Belgium are in third on six and Turkiye are bottom on zero.

Among the players hoping to impress Mancini during the next national team camp, which officially begins on Monday (November 9), will be 17-year-old central midfielder Cassano, who has earned his first Italy call-up before making a competitive appearance for Como.

The teenager was only promoted to the Como U21 squad at the beginning of the 2026-27 season and only earned his first caps for the Italy U18 squad in September.

A post shared by riccardocassano (@richi.cassa)

The youngster did train and travel with the senior Como squad during pre-season, but his only appearances this season have been with the Primavera league and in the UEFA Youth League.

This is not the first time that Mancini has given opportunities to players who have been previously untested in Serie A: Nicolo Zaniolo, who has also been included in the November squad, was handed his first cap for the senior national team by Mancini back in 2019, six months before his first competitive appearance with Roma.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

Good on him we need to give the young kids experience (and stick with them if they have the long term potential) regardless of the short term pain.

#1306. How Declan Rice's new role has turned him into the Premier League assist king, saves him from burnout and reduces Arsenal's reliance on set-piece goals

Published: 12:00 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:00 EDT, 5 November 2026

For so long, Declan Rice was Mikel Arteta’s lighthouse. ‘You just look at him and you know where to head,’ said the Arsenal boss. ‘A focal point giving clarity and direction to everybody.’

Only, not any more. Arteta had a chat with his midfield general at the start of the season, one Rice described as a ‘really honest conversation’, to discuss how he wanted his role to evolve.

After setting up Kai Havertz’s winner against Liverpool with a superb overlap run and cross on Sunday, Rice revealed what Arteta had told him.

‘I’ve done well but he believes I can still do more and he's drilled that into me,’ said Rice. ‘This season I've really tried to attack that part going forward, trying to come up with assists, create chances, create moments. Being behind the ball as well, linking the play. Being involved with all aspects, for me, is my best position.’

He’s certainly doing the creative part of that assignment. Rice’s assist for Havertz at Anfield was his fifth of the season, the most of any player in the Premier League, and puts him on track to obliterate his previous high of eight in 2023-24. Remarkably, for the corner specialist at the league's renowned set-piece kings, all five have come from open play.

Rice, too, revealed he’d discussed overlapping before the Liverpool game and told Havertz to attack balls into the box. That’s just what they both did.

Arsenal's Declan Rice is top of the assist charts in the Premier League this season with five

His latest came at Anfield on Sunday when he made an overlapping run around Noni Madueke who picks up the ball on the edge of the box...

...Madueke plays the ball into Rice's path and he crosses for Kai Havertz (arm raised) to finish at the back post

In truth, Rice’s role has evolved throughout his time at Arsenal.

In the very early days at the Emirates, Rice spent most of his time sitting in a defensive midfield role.

As the seasons have progressed, especially after Martin Zubimendi’s arrival last summer, Rice has been freed to drive further up the pitch, and occupy that space in the left channel.

You can see from his heat map over his Arsenal career, where the redder zones reflect more touches in that area, how much that role has shifted.

In his first season at Arsenal, Rice pops up all over the pitch...

...the following year he appears as an attacking force on the left side of the pitch...

...as he did again last season alongside Martin Zubimendi when Arsenal went on to win the title...

...but this season he is popping up more on the right-hand side, as seen at Anfield for Havertz's winning goal

What’s most noticeable about this season, following the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes and Arteta’s ability to use converted left back Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield, is that Rice has now shifted to the right.

That has enabled him to link up more effectively with Bukayo Saka or Noni Madueke on that side.

What is perhaps less obvious, but even more telling, is that despite the sight of Rice bursting into the box on the overlap down the right to set up Havertz, he is actually doing most of his creative work and tempo-setting from deeper on the pitch.

As Rice put it, ‘Being behind the ball as well’.

Early in this campaign, he spent a large portion of games picking up possession between Arsenal's centre backs, allowing the champions to create overloads when building up play and bypass an opposition press.

He’s averaging just one touch in the opposition box per game in the league, the lowest number in any season of his Arsenal career. He’s only played a handful of passes all season beyond the edge of the 18-yard box.

In Arsenal’s victory over Sunderland, in which Rice set up one goal and created another two chances, he was the deepest sitting of all Arteta’s midfielders (No 41)

And yet it’s making him more influential than ever. He’s playing more forward passes than in any season at the club. More passes into the final third, more line-breaking passes. And he's carrying the ball towards goal more frequently than at any point in his Arsenal career.

At the same time, he’s having less defensive responsibility, averaging the fewest ball recoveries and possession wins in the final third of any of his seasons at the club.

There is a small caveat to add here. For as clearly effective and influential as he has been in this evolved role, Rice is still overperforming his numbers a little.

His five assists have come from a total open-play expected assists (xA) tally of just 1.07. No one has overperformed that metric – which measures how likely the chances you’ve created are to result in a goal – as much as Rice.

You only need to look back at a few of those assists this season. His one for Madueke against Nottingham Forest was a simple pass out to the touchline where the winger then did all the work to cut inside and bend a beauty into the far corner.

He did the same for Havertz on the other flank for his equaliser against Chelsea. And it was a little sideways pass to Guimaraes against Sunderland that his midfield partner then whacked into the top corner from long range.

By contrast, Martin Odegaard, for so long his side’s creative hub, is yet to claim an assist from open play despite having an xA of 1.9, the fourth-highest in the division.

But that is not to take away from the superb work Rice is doing. Where he’s really showing his expertise is in how simply he’s making those forward creative passes look. Take these examples:

After his assist at Anfield, Rice creates another chance for Jurrien Timber, poking a little pass that cuts out two Liverpool players to open up space for a long-range shot

Against Everton, he knocks another through the lines into space for Madueke to turn and run on to

And even though Havertz still had everything to do for his goal against Chelsea, Rice’s pass to him takes out four blue shirts

The xA on the above pass might not be high but it creates the opportunity for Havertz to conjure some magic. Short, simple passes that help open up defences.

Rice is doing all this while running less, too. He’s averaging 6.8 miles per game. Over the previous two campaigns, he travelled 7.1.

Perhaps it was always going to have to be this way. It was over the World Cup this summer that the sheer weight of games Rice had played in 2025-26 – 69 for club and country – finally took its toll.

He played through a hamstring injury from Christmas onwards and was substituted early in England’s victory over Croatia with ‘neural pain’ in his back.

'The body's been through a lot this season,’ he said after the semi-final defeat by Argentina. 'I think you can see I'm mentally done, physically done. I need a break now.’

Now, with the likes of Guimaraes and Lewis-Skelly as well as Zubimendi around him, Rice is able to keep starting every game but also do what great midfield metronomes like Rodri and Paul Scholes did before him: control matches without having to bust a gut.

It has allowed Rice to be more selective in his runs forward. Guimaraes, especially, is dynamic enough to sit in for those moments – like at Anfield – when Rice spots the opportunity to make his move.

Rice's movement and backheel allowed space for Bruno Guimaraes to fire in the winning goal against Leeds last month

He did similar against Leeds to set up Guimaraes’ winner, charging into the box to play a neat little backheel to the Brazilian, who fired into the bottom corner.

It allows Arteta, too, to find different ways to open up defences in open play, whether they are sitting deep or pressing man-to-man. Rice is now able to exploit the gaps or pick the locks.

Arsenal have not always had this luxury and, when they frequently struggled to do so in the past, had to turn to set-pieces. Not any more.

Rice may no longer be Arteta's lighthouse but he continues to find new ways to lead Arsenal to glory.
